title: Operation AMÓN: Military Kills Eight Calarcá Dissidents in Guaviare Bombing-Raid
detail: Colombia's armed forces killed eight fighters from the FARC-EP dissident faction led by alias 'Calarcá' — specifically the Jorge Suárez Briceño Bloc and Rodrigo Cadete structure — in a pre-dawn operation near El Retorno, Guaviare, President de la Espriella announced. Code-named Operation AMÓN, the strike combined a precision bombing run by five Kfir fighter jets and six Super Tucano aircraft with a follow-up commando raid by Joint Special Operations Command troops, who seized more than a dozen rifles and five machine guns. 'Colombia must know that we are going on the offensive,' de la Espriella said, warning dissident commanders 'will have nowhere to hide and no sanctuary anywhere in the national territory.' The government presented the strike as the first of 15 planned operations targeting armed-group leadership within its first 100 days.

media.caption: Colombian Army forces conduct an offensive against FARC dissidents

title: De la Espriella Orders New Round of Drug-Trafficking Extraditions to the US
detail: As part of the same August 27 security push that produced the Guaviare strike on Calarcá dissidents, the de la Espriella government ordered a fresh round of extraditions of alleged drug traffickers to the United States, continuing Colombia's cooperation with US federal prosecutors. The move follows a steady cadence of 2026 extraditions, including a Dominican-based cocaine and money-laundering ring leader sent to face charges in Puerto Rico and New Jersey, underscoring the new administration's emphasis on hardline security and counter-narcotics cooperation with Washington over the negotiated 'Total Peace' approach of predecessor Gustavo Petro.

media.caption: Colombia orders new extraditions of drug-trafficking suspects to the US
